set_title: Chronic liver disease signs: Caput medusae, Spider angiomas (spider nevi), Palmar erythema, Kayser-Fleischer rings and Terry nails
stem: A 16-year-old boy has 3 months of hand tremor, slurred speech and declining school performance. ALT and AST are elevated. Slit-lamp examination shows a golden-brown ring at the edge of each cornea.
oneliner: 16-year-old boy, tremor, slurred speech, high ALT + golden-brown ring at corneal edge → ?

whyNot.A: Caput medusae is abdominal wall veins; his finding is **a corneal ring**
whyNot.B: Spider angiomas are skin lesions; his finding is **a corneal ring**
whyNot.C: Palmar erythema is red palms; his finding is **in the cornea**
whyNot.E: Terry nails are white nail beds; his finding is **a corneal ring**

why: Copper deposits in Descemet membrane at the corneal edge. **Tremor, dysarthria and liver disease in a teenager** indicate Wilson disease.

idea.rule: Golden-brown corneal ring + liver and neurologic disease in a teen = Wilson disease.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus
Central arteriole with radiating red legs
White nail beds, narrow pink distal band

set_title: Neurocutaneous skin and eye signs: Cafe-au-lait macules, Crowe sign, Lisch nodules, Ash-leaf spots, Shagreen patch and Port-wine stain
stem: A 10-year-old girl has seven flat tan macules on her trunk. Examination also shows multiple tiny freckles in both axillae and the inguinal folds. Neurologic examination is normal.
oneliner: 10F, tan macules + tiny freckles in both axillae and groin → ?

whyNot.B: Lisch nodules are iris hamartomas; her finding is **axillary freckling**
whyNot.C: Ash-leaf spots are hypopigmented; her freckles are **dark, tiny and axillary**
whyNot.D: Shagreen patch is a leathery lower back plaque; she has **tiny axillary freckles**
whyNot.E: Port-wine stain is a flat purple facial stain; she has **axillary freckles**

why: Axillary or inguinal freckling is Crowe sign, a feature of neurofibromatosis type 1 that appears in early childhood. **Six or more tan macules plus axillary freckles** meet diagnostic criteria.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Freckles in the armpits or groin
Leathery orange-peel plaque on lower back
Flat purple facial stain along V1

idea.rule: Axillary or groin freckling = Crowe sign = neurofibromatosis type 1.
also: NF1 encodes neurofibromin, a Ras inhibitor

set_title: Neurocutaneous skin and eye signs: Cafe-au-lait macules, Crowe sign, Lisch nodules, Ash-leaf spots, Shagreen patch and Port-wine stain
stem: A 12-year-old boy has multiple tan macules and axillary freckling. A slit-lamp examination shows multiple well-defined, pigmented hamartomas of the iris (Lisch nodules).
oneliner: 12M, tan macules + pigmented iris hamartomas → gene?
ask: A mutation in which gene best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: NF2 causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas; he has **iris hamartomas and multiple tan macules**
whyNot.C: TSC2 causes hypopigmented ash-leaf spots; he has **tan macules and iris nodules**
whyNot.D: VHL causes retinal hemangioblastomas; he has **pigmented iris nodules**
whyNot.E: PTEN causes Cowden syndrome with trichilemmomas; he has **iris nodules with tan macules**

why: Pigmented iris hamartomas are Lisch nodules, found in nearly all adults with neurofibromatosis type 1. The **NF1 gene** on chromosome 17 encodes neurofibromin, a Ras inhibitor.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Freckles in the armpits or groin
Leathery orange-peel plaque on lower back
Flat purple facial stain along V1

idea.rule: Pigmented iris hamartomas = Lisch nodules = NF1 mutation (neurofibromin).
also: Optic glioma and pheochromocytoma also occur

set_title: Eye findings in syndromes: Brushfield spots, Upward lens dislocation, Downward lens dislocation, Blue sclerae and Leukocoria
stem: A newborn boy has hypotonia and upslanting palpebral fissures. Examination of the iris shows small white speckles around its periphery.
oneliner: Newborn boy, hypotonia + upslanting eyes + white speckles at iris periphery → ?

whyNot.A: Upward lens dislocation is a displaced lens; his **iris has speckles**
whyNot.B: Downward lens dislocation shifts the lens; his finding is **iris speckling**
whyNot.C: Blue sclerae tint the white of the eye; his speckles are **on the iris**
whyNot.D: Leukocoria is a white pupillary reflex; his **pupil is not white**

why: White speckles on the peripheral iris are Brushfield spots, a feature of Down syndrome (trisomy 21), seen with upslanting eyes and hypotonia.

idea.rule: White iris speckles with hypotonia = Brushfield spots; Down syndrome.
also: Not seen in every Down syndrome patient

set_title: Eye findings in syndromes: Brushfield spots, Upward lens dislocation, Downward lens dislocation, Blue sclerae and Leukocoria
stem: A 17-year-old tall boy with long fingers and pectus excavatum has a lens displaced upward and outward on slit-lamp exam.
oneliner: 17M, tall, long fingers + lens displaced up and out → ?
ask: Which protein is most likely defective?

whyNot.B: Type I collagen defects cause brittle bones and **blue sclerae**, not upward lens shift
whyNot.C: Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency causes **downward** lens dislocation
whyNot.D: Elastin defects cause supravalvular aortic stenosis, not **lens displacement with long fingers**
whyNot.E: Type III collagen defects cause vascular Ehlers-Danlos, not **upward lens dislocation**

why: Upward and outward lens dislocation with a marfanoid habitus is Marfan syndrome, from a fibrillin-1 mutation weakening zonular fibers and the aortic wall.

idea.rule: Lens up and out + tall, long fingers = Marfan; fibrillin-1.

set_title: Eye findings in syndromes: Brushfield spots, Upward lens dislocation, Downward lens dislocation, Blue sclerae and Leukocoria
stem: A 15-year-old with intellectual disability and tall stature presents with a deep venous thrombosis. Slit-lamp exam shows a lens displaced downward and inward.
oneliner: 15M, intellectual disability, tall, DVT + lens displaced down and in → ?

whyNot.A: Phenylalanine builds up in phenylketonuria, with **musty odor and no lens dislocation or clotting**
whyNot.B: Tyrosine builds up in tyrosinemia, with **liver failure and no lens dislocation**
whyNot.D: Homogentisic acid builds up in alkaptonuria, with **dark urine and arthritis**
whyNot.E: Cysteine becomes **deficient** in this disorder, so it does not accumulate

why: Downward and inward lens dislocation with thrombosis and intellectual disability is homocystinuria. Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency raises homocysteine, which injures vessels.

idea.rule: Lens down and in + thrombosis + intellectual disability = homocysteine accumulation.
also: Treat with vitamin B6, low methionine diet

set_title: Newborn dysmorphic clues: Single palmar crease, Rocker-bottom feet, Overlapping clenched fingers, Short fourth and fifth metacarpals, Webbed neck and Cleft lip with polydactyly
stem: A small-for-gestational-age newborn boy has a prominent occiput and low-set ears. The soles of both feet bulge outward in the midfoot, and the heels project backward.
oneliner: Small newborn boy, prominent occiput, low-set ears + convex soles → ?

whyNot.A: A single palmar crease is on the hand; his finding is on the **feet**
whyNot.B: Overlapping fingers are a hand posture; his finding is **convex soles**
whyNot.C: Webbed neck is cervical skin folds; his finding is in the **feet**
whyNot.E: Cleft lip with polydactyly affects face and digits; his finding is **convex soles**

why: Convex soles with prominent heels are rocker-bottom feet, a feature of Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18) along with a prominent occiput and low-set ears.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Fists clenched, index over middle finger
Knuckles 4 and 5 missing in a fist
Loose skin folds from neck to shoulders

idea.rule: Convex soles with prominent heels = rocker-bottom feet; trisomy 18.
also: Usually fatal in the first year

set_title: Newborn dysmorphic clues: Single palmar crease, Rocker-bottom feet, Overlapping clenched fingers, Short fourth and fifth metacarpals, Webbed neck and Cleft lip with polydactyly
stem: A 15-year-old girl, 138 cm tall, has no breast development. Skin folds extend from the base of her ears to her shoulders, and her nipples are widely spaced.
oneliner: 15F, short, no breast development + neck skin folds, wide nipples → ?

whyNot.B: A single palmar crease is on the palm; hers are **neck skin folds**
whyNot.C: Rocker-bottom feet are convex soles; her finding is **at the neck**
whyNot.D: Short metacarpals show depressed knuckles; her findings are **skin folds on the neck**
whyNot.E: Cleft lip with polydactyly affects face and digits; she has **neck skin folds**

why: Loose skin folds from neck to shoulders are a webbed neck, from fetal cystic hygroma, a feature of Turner syndrome (45,X).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Fists clenched, index over middle finger
Knuckles 4 and 5 missing in a fist
Loose skin folds from neck to shoulders

idea.rule: Neck skin folds with short stature, no puberty = Turner syndrome.
also: Check for coarctation and bicuspid aortic valve

set_title: Newborn dysmorphic clues: Single palmar crease, Rocker-bottom feet, Overlapping clenched fingers, Short fourth and fifth metacarpals, Webbed neck and Cleft lip with polydactyly
stem: A newborn girl has cleft lip and palate, postaxial polydactyly, microphthalmia and a scalp skin defect.
oneliner: Newborn girl, cleft lip and palate, extra digits, microphthalmia, scalp defect → ?
ask: Which chromosomal abnormality is most likely?

whyNot.A: Trisomy 18 gives rocker-bottom feet and clenched fists, not **cleft lip with polydactyly**
whyNot.B: Trisomy 21 gives hypotonia and upslanting eyes, not **polydactyly with scalp defect**
whyNot.C: Monosomy X gives webbed neck and short stature, not **cleft lip with polydactyly**
whyNot.E: 22q11.2 deletion gives conotruncal defects and hypocalcemia, not **polydactyly and scalp defect**

why: Cleft lip and palate, polydactyly, microphthalmia and scalp defects are the classic Patau syndrome (trisomy 13) pattern, often with holoprosencephaly.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Fists clenched, index over middle finger
Knuckles 4 and 5 missing in a fist
Loose skin folds from neck to shoulders

idea.rule: Cleft lip, polydactyly, scalp defect = Patau, trisomy 13.

set_title: Congenital infection signs: Hutchinson teeth, Mulberry molars, Saddle nose, Saber shins and Blueberry muffin rash
stem: A 2-day-old girl born at 36 weeks has a continuous machine-like murmur, cloudy lenses and failed hearing screening. Temperature is 37.0°C. Her skin has many firm blue-purple papules, and her liver and spleen are enlarged.
oneliner: 2-day-old F, cataracts + PDA murmur + blue-purple skin papules → ?
ask: What best explains the skin lesions?

whyNot.A: Maternal antiplatelet antibodies cause petechiae, not **cataracts and a continuous murmur**
whyNot.C: Septic emboli bring fever and shock; her **temperature is normal**
whyNot.D: Vasculitis is rare in neonates; **cataracts and PDA** point to congenital infection
whyNot.E: Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding, not **blue-purple papules with cataracts**

why: Blue-purple papules in a newborn with **cataracts and a PDA murmur** are blueberry muffin lesions: dermal extramedullary hematopoiesis from congenital rubella (or CMV).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: First molars with many small cusps

idea.rule: Newborn purple papules + infection stigmata = dermal hematopoiesis (congenital rubella or CMV).

set_title: Nutrition deficiency signs: Bitot spots, Corkscrew hairs, Casal necklace, Rachitic rosary and Flaky paint dermatosis
stem: A 4-year-old boy from a rural area has had poor vision in dim light for 3 months. His diet lacks vegetables and dairy. Examination shows dry conjunctivae with triangular, foamy, gray-white patches at the temporal limbus.
oneliner: 4yo M, night blindness + malnutrition + foamy gray conjunctival patches → ?

whyNot.A: Corkscrew hairs come with gum bleeding; he has **night blindness** and conjunctival patches
whyNot.B: Casal necklace is a neck rash; his lesions are **on the conjunctiva**
whyNot.C: Rachitic rosary is rib beading; his findings are **ocular**
whyNot.E: Flaky paint dermatosis needs edema and skin peeling; he has **eye findings**

why: Foamy gray conjunctival patches are Bitot spots, keratinized epithelium from vitamin A deficiency; **night blindness** is the earliest symptom.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Peeling patches with edema and big belly

idea.rule: Foamy conjunctival patch + night blindness = Bitot spot of vitamin A deficiency.
also: Vitamin A forms retinal for rhodopsin

set_title: Nutrition deficiency signs: Bitot spots, Corkscrew hairs, Casal necklace, Rachitic rosary and Flaky paint dermatosis
stem: A 40-year-old man from a region where corn is the staple has had 3 weeks of diarrhea and confusion. A sharply demarcated, scaly, sun-exposed rash encircles his neck.
oneliner: 40M, corn-based diet + diarrhea + confusion + sun-exposed neck rash → ?
ask: Which vitamin deficiency best explains this rash?

whyNot.A: Thiamine deficiency causes ataxia and ophthalmoplegia, not a **sun-exposed neck rash**
whyNot.B: Riboflavin deficiency causes cheilosis and glossitis, not **diarrhea with a photosensitive rash**
whyNot.C: Pyridoxine deficiency causes neuropathy and seizures, not **photosensitive rash with diarrhea**
whyNot.E: B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and neuropathy, not a **sun-exposed rash**

why: Diarrhea, dementia and a **sun-exposed rash around the neck** (Casal necklace) are pellagra from niacin (B3) deficiency; corn has little bioavailable niacin.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Peeling patches with edema and big belly

idea.rule: Diarrhea + dementia + photosensitive neck rash = pellagra, niacin deficiency.
also: Causes: corn diet, carcinoid, Hartnup, isoniazid

set_title: Odor clues: Fruity breath, Fetor hepaticus, Bitter almond odor, Garlic odor, Musty (mousy) body odor and Maple syrup urine
stem: A 6-day-old girl born at term has had poor feeding, vomiting and progressive lethargy for 2 days. She is hypotonic with intermittent opisthotonus. Her diapers and ear wax smell like burnt sugar.
oneliner: 6-day-old F, poor feeding + lethargy + hypotonia + burnt-sugar urine → ?

whyNot.A: Fruity breath is acetone in ketoacidosis; her smell is **burnt sugar in a newborn**
whyNot.C: Fetor hepaticus is a liver-failure breath odor, not **urine smelling of burnt sugar**
whyNot.D: Garlic odor suggests toxin exposure, not **burnt-sugar urine in a newborn**
whyNot.E: Musty odor is PKU, which presents later; her smell is **burnt sugar**

why: **Burnt-sugar urine** with neonatal encephalopathy is maple syrup urine disease: deficient branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase lets leucine, isoleucine and valine ketoacids accumulate.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Musty smell of urine and sweat

idea.rule: Sweet burnt-sugar urine + newborn lethargy = MSUD, BCKDH deficiency.
also: Restrict leucine, isoleucine, valine; thiamine helps

set_title: Odor clues: Fruity breath, Fetor hepaticus, Bitter almond odor, Garlic odor, Musty (mousy) body odor and Maple syrup urine
stem: A 10-month-old boy adopted from abroad has developmental delay, eczema and recent seizures. He has fair skin, blond hair and blue eyes, and his urine and sweat have a musty odor.
oneliner: 10-month-old M, developmental delay + seizures + fair skin + musty odor → ?
ask: Which enzyme deficiency best explains this presentation?

whyNot.A: Tyrosinase deficiency causes albinism without **developmental delay and musty odor**
whyNot.B: That causes dark urine on standing and arthritis, not **musty odor with seizures**
whyNot.D: That gives burnt-sugar urine and a neonatal crisis, not **musty odor in infancy**
whyNot.E: That causes lens dislocation and thrombosis, not **fair skin with a musty odor**

why: A **musty odor with fair skin, eczema and seizures** shows phenylketonuria: without phenylalanine hydroxylase, phenylalanine cannot become tyrosine, so melanin falls.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Musty smell of urine and sweat

idea.rule: Musty odor + fair skin + developmental delay = PKU, phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency.
